concept.name: Delivery month
concept.definition: The specified month within which a futures contract matures and can be settled by delivery, or within which the delivery period begins, as defined in the contract specification.
concept.intuition: The delivery month is the contract's calendar label: 'December corn' means the corn future whose obligations fall due in December.
concept.mechanics: Exchanges list a cycle of delivery months per product (e.g., March, May, July, September, December for many grains). Each month trades as a distinct contract with its own price and open interest; the nearest is the spot/front month, later ones are back months, and prices across months embed carrying costs (contango) or discounts (backwardation).
concept.failure_modes: Liquidity migrates from the front month to the next month well before expiry, so trading the wrong month late in its life means wide spreads and delivery risk; confusing the delivery month with the last trading day (which usually precedes it) is a common operational error.
concept.misconceptions: The delivery month is not a single date but a window: the exact first/last trading and notice days are set per product and can fall in the prior month.
concept.example: A trader long 'ZCZ25' holds December 2025 corn futures; as December approaches, volume and open interest shift to the March 2026 contract, prompting most traders to roll rather than risk delivery.
